points.description: Role: the learning rate controls the speed of convergence (the step size taken along the negative gradient). A low rate gives slow, overdamped convergence; a high rate gives faster but underdamped, zigzagging convergence. Equivalent wording, such as 'it sets how big each step is and so how quickly it reaches the minimum', earns the mark.

Danger: if the learning rate exceeds a critical value, learning becomes unstable (the updates overshoot and diverge rather than converging). Equivalent wording, such as 'the weights oscillate out of control or blow up', earns the mark. Saying only that a high rate is 'bad' without mentioning instability or divergence does not earn it.
